name: NavbarItem
description: Text element of a navigation bar that leads to a section of the application. It shows whether it is the current page or section and responds to the cursor with a soft background. Text only: it has no icon.

dos: Short label, one or two words, that says where it leads: "Home", "Projects".
Mark `active` only on the element of the current section, so people know where they are. Only one can be active at a time.
Group them in a navigation list (`nav` with a list) and leave order and spacing to the container.
The background change on hover is handled by the browser with `:hover`: do not force it with a prop.

donts.case: Running an action that does not navigate (open a menu, save, sign out)
donts.why: A navigation item leads somewhere else; a button runs an action. They are announced differently and activated with different keys.

donts.case: Link inside a paragraph or running text
donts.why: Link is designed for running text, with underline and the same size as the surrounding text. NavbarItem has a background and bar height.

donts.case: Icon-only action in the bar (search, profile, notifications)
donts.why: NavbarItem only supports text. Without a visible label, the element has no accessible name.

donts.case: Label of several sentences or one that does not fit in the bar
donts.why: The element does not wrap its text (Figma: auto width). A long sentence breaks the bar and does not read as a menu option.

related.difference: Link is inline text inside a paragraph; NavbarItem is a bar element with a background and fixed height.
Runs an action; NavbarItem navigates to a section.
Icon-only button for bar actions; NavbarItem has text only.
The Navbar bar groups NavbarItems in its navigation list.

props.name: label
props.description: Element text. It is the only content: it does not allow icons or other components. Default text in Figma: "Home".
props.usage: label="Projects" inside an element with href="/projects" (via asChild)

props.name: active
props.description: If true, marks the element as the current page or section: accent-alpha.3 background and accent.11 text. In Figma it is the "active" value of the state property; the "default" value is equivalent to false.
props.usage: active with label="Home" for the current section

controlled.name: active
controlled.description: Current section. Painted with the accent background and text and announced as the current location.

root.description: Root element. It is an `<a>` that receives the destination through `asChild` (see composition.asChild). It takes the bar's height and fits the text in width.

label.description: Element text. A single line, no wrapping.

height.note: A single size. In Figma, the height is the variable tokens/space/menu-item-height-2 (32 px).

modes.hug: Fits the text plus 12 px of padding on each side (61 px with "Home").

width.note: In Figma the width is automatic (HUG). If the bar needs equal-width elements, this component does not solve that.

autoLayout.gap: Not applicable: single child (itemSpacing 0 in Figma).

a11y.role: link (implicit from the a element with href, which the consumer passes with asChild)
a11y.name: The label text. It must make sense outside the bar.
keyboard: Tab — moves focus to the element
a11y.focusIndicator: Double ring with :focus-visible: 4px outer with colors.accent.accent-alpha.8 and 2px inner with colors.accent.accent.3. Not in Figma: copied from Button's ring.
a11y.minTarget: 32 px tall (menu-item-height-2), above 24×24 px (WCAG 2.5.8). The width depends on the text.
a11y.contrastNote: neutral.11 text on the bar background at rest; neutral.12 on hover; accent.11 on accent-alpha.3 when active. ≥ 4.5:1 for normal text. Not measured in Figma.

label.voice: Short and direct, says where it leads: "Home", "Projects", "Settings".

behavior.overflow: nowrap: the text is not cut or wrapped. In Figma, the width is automatic.

i18n.rtl: The padding is symmetric and the text is centered: it does not change in RTL. The order of the elements is decided by the container.
i18n.textExpansion: With text 30-40 % longer, the element grows in width (HUG). It may push other elements in the bar: the container must plan for the space.

cases: renders an `<a>` that receives the href through asChild; without href it is not a link
active=true applies aria-current="page" and the byActive.true tokens
active=false has no aria-current and uses the byActive.false tokens
hover (only with active=false) uses colors.neutral.neutral-alpha.3 and colors.neutral.neutral.12
the text does not wrap: the width grows with the content
the height is 32 px with tokens.space.menu-item-height-2 and the horizontal padding is spacing.3
visible focus uses the double ring from tokens.bindings.base

needsReview: Figma has 3 variants (state=default, hover, active) and no other axis. All 3 were read: background, text, height, padding and radius bound to variables in all of them.

state=hover is not a prop: hover is native (:hover) and handled with CSS. Proposed decision: do not add a prop for hover, which respects AGENTS.md (native states with CSS). If the design needs a fixed hover for documentation, decide it here.
state=active is exposed as the boolean prop `active` (aria-current="page"). Proposed decision: the name `active` instead of `state`, because it is a controlled usage state (current section).

Root element `a` with href via asChild. Figma does not say whether the element navigates or runs something, nor which element to use. Proposed decision: `a`, because it is a navigation element. If in the product it is a button that opens something, change semantics and the dont's.
No variable in Figma: none. All measurements and colors of the 3 variants are bound to variables (tokens/space/menu-item-height-2, spacing/3, radius/2, colors/*, text-style/2/medium).
:active state (pressed) listed in states.native, but not designed in Figma. It is painted with the same style as hover or not painted: decide.

Active state with hover is not designed: byActive.true only defines default. With native :hover, the active element may change background on mouse over: decide whether it should keep the active background.
Focus ring (focusRingOuter / focusRingInner): not in Figma. Copied from Button's ring (4 px accent-alpha.8 and 2 px accent.3). Verify by hand.
Default label value: "Home" (default text in Figma). Proposed decision: keep it, but in code an empty label would be a usage error; consider `required: true`.
content.label.maxLength: 20 is a proposed decision, not read from Figma. The text of the 3 variants is "Home" (37 px wide).
behavior.overflow: there is no truncation in Figma (auto width). Left as nowrap. If the bar needs to truncate on mobile, define it.
Contrast not measured. Figma has no disabled or loading states: they were not documented.

Descriptions, guidance, a11y, testing and content: written as a draft, they do not come from Figma. Decisions I made: do not wrap the text, no icon, dont's from Button/Link/IconButton, anchors.figma.node points to the COMPONENT_SET (29:1408), not to a variant.
governance: null, same as Button. Component owners still need to be defined.
No code props without a Figma equivalent were added (e.g. href, onClick). The destination is passed through asChild so as not to add props the contract does not have.
